half: producer cost, live draw path, player visibility

producer_live.visibility: detection: visible entity ids supplied per frame, fog predicates for effects and shots

motion_proof.note: two frames read 1.2 s apart from one live ring

what_this_shows: A player-visible frame (638 of 752 hulls) built from a running GameManager draws in the reviewed W01 path: 54 producer frames adopted, 0 dropped, decode 0.716 ms, frames behind median 0 / p95 0 / p99 1 against a limit of 2.

The producer's gather+pack+publish is inside its 1.0 ms budget at a combat steady state: 0.964 ms median over 60 reps for 736 instances and 1,426 transients (all-visible), 0.964 ms for the 634-instance player-visible frame of the same tick.
The live producer measured 1.10 ms median over 152 frames - above the bench figure because it runs a different tick and includes the ring publish.
Replacing the transient generator with a direct pack loop took the same frame from 2.6 ms to 0.96-1.02 ms (2.6x, interleaved A/B in one process on identical state).
The picture is live: two reads 1.2 s apart differ in 96 ship positions and in transient count.
what_this_does_not_show: Not a frame rate. The producer is limited by the Python simulation: 179 ms per tick median, 442 ms p95 here, so the stream runs at 3.0 Hz.

Computing what the player can see cost 105 ms per frame (42 ms entity sensors + 74 ms fog predicates on transients). That is renderer work the bridge receives, not bridge cost; the C++ path should filter transients against the fog mask rather than querying per effect.
No fog, HUD, planets, transients drawn, or input in the window; it draws hulls only.
Nothing on Windows/D3D12; CI is disabled by the owner, so no CI check exists for this head.
